verdict.rationale: Moss documents upserting and deleting documents in an index, and real-time sessions that index and query locally before syncing to the cloud. It also claims indexes "stay fresh" via zero-downtime hot-swaps, with snapshot fallback when the cloud is unreachable. However, the evidence never states how quickly upserts or deletes appear in search results, nor gives a consistency model. missing for 10: documented propagation latency or freshness guarantees for upserts and deletes, an explicit consistency model (read-after-write, eventual), behavior under continuous high-rate writes, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can upsert and delete records continuously and have changes reflected in search results quickly, with documented freshness/consistency behavior

citations.quote: Upsert more docs later ... Fetch specific docs ... Delete docs or the index when done
index and query locally during a conversation, then sync to the cloud
Hydrate from the cloud and stay fresh with zero-downtime hot-swaps.
If the cloud is unreachable or answers with a temporary error, such as a 429 or 503, the load serves the snapshot instead of failing.
